rules: Only your one piece moves. The other pieces stay where they are.
Your own pieces block the way and cannot be captured. You may capture a piece of the other colour by landing on it; a pawn captures only diagonally.
A king never steps onto a square an enemy piece attacks.
Reach the marked square within the move budget shown. When the task says "fewest moves", only a shortest route fits the budget.
entries.summary: Move one piece to the marked square, going around the pieces in the way.
entries.title: Reach the Target

rules: An attack follows how a piece captures: pawns attack diagonally forward, knights jump, and rooks, bishops and queens attack along open lines.
A line stops at the first piece in the way. A pinned piece still attacks its squares.
Select the pieces, then choose Submit. Choose None if no piece attacks the square.
entries.summary: Select every piece of the named colour that attacks the marked square.
entries.title: Find the Attackers

rules: This is a normal chess position: every chess rule applies.
Checkmate is check with no legal way out: the king has no safe square, the check cannot be blocked, and the checking piece cannot be captured.
A move that is not legal here is not played and does not count as an answer.
entries.summary: Find a move that gives checkmate now. Any checkmating move counts.
entries.title: Mate in One

rules: Reach the far rank, capture every opposing pawn, or leave the opponent without a move.
Pawns move forward and capture diagonally. A pawn on its starting rank may advance two empty squares.
No en passant. Pawns stay pawns at the far rank.
Three repeated positions or 40 turns without a capture or pawn move draw this mini-game.
entries.summary: The original Pawn Duel mini-game, with its own simplified rules.
entries.title: Pawn Duel

rules: This is a normal chess position, and it is the king's side to move.
A king may not move onto a square an enemy piece attacks, or next to the other king. It may capture an enemy piece that is not protected.
There is no castling in these positions. Choose None if the king has no legal move.
entries.summary: Select every square the king to move can legally go to.
entries.title: King Safe Squares

rules: This is a normal chess position: every chess rule applies.
Get out of check by moving the king, blocking the check, or capturing the checking piece. Every legal escape counts.
A move that leaves your king in check, or breaks how a piece moves, is a wrong answer here. The board does not change.
entries.summary: Your king is in check. Play any legal move that gets out of check.
entries.title: Escape Check

rules: Only rooks move. Capture every opposing pawn to win. Losing all your moving pieces or having no move loses.
Three repeated positions or 40 turns without a capture or pawn move draw this mini-game.
entries.summary: The original Rook Sweep mini-game, with its own simplified rules.
entries.title: Rook Sweep

rules: Only bishops move. Capture every opposing pawn to win. Losing all your moving pieces or having no move loses.
Three repeated positions or 40 turns without a capture or pawn move draw this mini-game.
entries.summary: The original Bishop Sweep mini-game, with its own simplified rules.
entries.title: Bishop Sweep

rules: Win by capturing every opposing piece, or by reaching the far rank with a pawn that is still there after your opponent replies. You lose if you have no move. Pawns never promote, and there is no en passant.
Three repeated positions or 40 turns without a capture or pawn move draw this mini-game.
entries.summary: The original Rooks and Pawns mini-game, with its own simplified rules.
entries.title: Rooks and Pawns

rules: Win by capturing every opposing piece, or by reaching the far rank with a pawn that is still there after your opponent replies. You lose if you have no move. Pawns never promote, and there is no en passant.
Three repeated positions or 40 turns without a capture or pawn move draw this mini-game.
entries.summary: The original Bishops and Pawns mini-game, with its own simplified rules.
entries.title: Bishops and Pawns

rules: Win by capturing every opposing piece, or by reaching the far rank with a pawn that is still there after your opponent replies. You lose if you have no move. Pawns never promote, and there is no en passant.
Three repeated positions or 40 turns without a capture or pawn move draw this mini-game.
entries.summary: The original Queen Against Pawns mini-game: one black queen against eight white pawns.
entries.title: Queen Against Pawns

rules: Only knights move. Capture every other piece. You lose if your knight is captured or cannot move.
Three repeated positions or 40 turns without a capture or pawn move draw this mini-game.
entries.summary: The original Knight Capture mini-game, with its own simplified rules.
entries.title: Knight Capture

rules: Visit a8, h8 and h1, then return to a1. Avoid the black pawns and the squares they attack.
entries.summary: The original Knight Corners route: visit the corners in order with the white knight.
entries.title: Knight Corners

rules: A piece protects a friend when it could capture on that square if an enemy piece took the friend there.
Pawns protect diagonally forward, knights jump, and rooks, bishops and queens protect along open lines. A pinned piece still protects its squares.
Select the pieces, then choose Submit. Choose None if nothing protects the piece.
entries.summary: Select every piece that protects the marked piece.
entries.title: Find the Defenders

rules: Checkmate: in check with no legal move. Stalemate: not in check, with no legal move; the game is drawn.
Check: the king is attacked but has a legal way out. Neither: none of these three.
"Neither" does not mean the game cannot be drawn some other way.
entries.summary: Decide whether the side to move is checkmated, stalemated, in check, or none of these.
entries.title: Check, Mate or Stalemate?

rules: This is a normal chess position: every chess rule applies.
A piece is safe when the opponent cannot win material from it within the short look-ahead described in the task, counting recaptures.
You can move the piece away, protect it, capture the attacker, or block the attack. Any move that meets the goal counts.
entries.summary: An enemy piece threatens one of yours. Find a move that keeps it safe.
entries.title: Save Your Piece

rules: Count with the usual values: queen 9, rook 5, bishop 3, knight 3, pawn 1.
Before you capture, look at every recapture. Taking a protected piece with a more valuable one can lose material.
Sometimes the best choice is not to capture at all.
entries.summary: Decide whether a capture wins material, loses it, or only trades.
entries.title: Capture Wisely

rules: Castling: the king moves two squares toward a rook that has not moved; the squares between are empty, the king is not in check, and it does not pass through or land on an attacked square.
Promotion: a pawn reaching the last rank becomes a queen, rook, bishop or knight.
En passant: a pawn that has just moved two squares can be captured as if it had moved one, but only immediately.
entries.summary: Castling, promotion and en passant: play them correctly and know when they are not allowed.
entries.title: Special Moves

rules: A fork attacks two or more targets at once. A pin holds a piece in front of a more valuable one behind it.
Not every fork or pin wins material: check every reply the opponent has.
A mating threat is a move that would give checkmate next turn if the opponent did nothing about it.
entries.summary: Spot and use forks and pins, and create or stop a checkmate threat.
entries.title: Simple Tactics

rules: This is a normal chess game against a computer defender that plays legal moves.
Win only by checkmate. Stalemate is a draw, and losing your queen or rook ends the task.
Threefold repetition and the 50-move rule can be claimed as draws; fivefold repetition and the 75-move rule end the game automatically.
entries.summary: Checkmate a lone king with a queen or a rook and your king.
entries.title: Finish the Game

rules: Each task states a goal, such as winning material or stopping an immediate loss, but not the theme.
Any move that meets the stated goal counts, even if it is not the move the author expected.
Some positions need no capture, no special move and no tactic.
entries.summary: Positions without a topic label: work out what matters, then act.
entries.title: Mixed Practice

rules: This is a normal chess game against a gentle computer opponent that makes mistakes.
Notes on your moves, such as castling or developing your pieces, are things worth reviewing, not wrong answers.
End the game whenever you like. A missed or allowed checkmate becomes a moment you can try again.
entries.summary: Play a short, ordinary game from a reviewed start, then look again at a moment from it.
entries.title: Guided Games

rules: This is a normal chess game against a computer defender that plays legal moves.
Win by promoting your pawn and keeping the new piece: it must still be on the board after your opponent's reply. A promotion that gives checkmate wins at once.
Losing the pawn, a stalemate, a draw, or a new piece captured at once ends the task.
entries.summary: Promote your one pawn against the lone king, and keep the new piece.
entries.title: Pawn Race

rules: This is a normal chess game with only kings and pawns, against a computer opponent.
Win only by checkmate: promote a pawn to get a piece that can give mate. Stalemate and every other draw end the task.
Threefold repetition and the 50-move rule can be claimed as draws; fivefold repetition and the 75-move rule end the game automatically.
entries.summary: Kings and eight pawns each: make a passed pawn, promote it and give checkmate.
entries.title: Pawn War with Kings

rules: This is a normal chess game with kings, pawns and one kind of piece for each side, against a computer opponent.
Win only by checkmate. Stalemate and every other draw end the task. Castling and en passant follow the normal rules.
Threefold repetition and the 50-move rule can be claimed as draws; fivefold repetition and the 75-move rule end the game automatically.
entries.summary: Kings, pawns and one kind of piece each: play a whole game to checkmate.
entries.title: Cut-Down Chess

rules: This is a normal chess game against a computer defender that plays legal moves.
Win only by checkmate. Stalemate is a draw, and losing a bishop ends the task: one bishop cannot mate.
Threefold repetition and the 50-move rule can be claimed as draws; fivefold repetition and the 75-move rule end the game automatically.
entries.summary: Checkmate a lone king with your king and two bishops.
entries.title: Two-Bishop Mate
